clue.text: Uncertainty around since business failure

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the doubting little word back to front

parts.note: an 'if' is a doubt or uncertainty, as in 'no ifs or buts'
as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Doubt has hung over the firm ever since its collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business failure' reads as one phrase, but 'business' is wordplay and only 'failure' defines; 'around' reverses the doubt word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating total flop, a complete failure.

clue.text: Ancestor following row embracing endless revolt

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: embracing means the rowing word holds the other letters

parts.note: you row with an oar

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to rebel is to revolt

explanation.surface: A forefather pursued a quarrel that included a never-ending uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but is the rowing kind, giving OAR; REBEL less its end is REBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is a forefather, someone you are descended from.

clue.text: Usual upset about fellow ignoring a former student

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the other piece
upset means the letters of usual are knocked into a new order
ignoring means the letter A is left out of the word

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: An unusual chap overlooks a student from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a former student' tempts as the definition, but 'a' is the letter that 'ignoring' drops from the fellow; 'upset' scrambles Usual around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or past pupil of a school or college.

clue.text: Head that is higher than foot in sequence

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the sequence word

parts.note: a chain is a sequence

indicators.note: in a down clue, higher than places one piece above, before, the other

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: In a line, the head is naturally above the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the leader or head of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Turning crazy, pressure brought about decline in form

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
rot is decay, a decline

indicators.note: Turning signals that the word for mad is read backwards

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A mind going mad under strain brings on a decline in performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes OCOL from LOCO. 'brought about' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the correct procedure or etiquette, i.e. proper form.

clue.text: Music by thrush led man to be distracted

indicators.note: to be distracted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A songbird led a man astray with its music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm and blues is a genre of popular music rooted in African American blues.

clue.text: Drum cheers British soldiers

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Drums applaud the British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabor is a small drum played with one hand, often alongside a pipe.

clue.text: Wreath quietly placed in wooden building

indicators.note: placed in means the soft letter goes inside the building

parts.note: a chalet is a wooden house, as in the Alps
P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: A garland hung softly in a timber cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or wreath worn on the head.

clue.text: Pretentious piece of marketing in top area

indicators.note: in means the advert goes inside the cover

parts.note: a lid is a top
an ad is an advert, a piece of marketing

explanation.surface: A showy advert in a prime spot.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da is an informal word for affected and snobbish, pretentious.

clue.text: Catch up with leader supporting bit of change: in US security system

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means this piece sits below the rest

parts.note: a cent is an American coin, a bit of change in the US

indicators.note: up reverses the word in a down clue, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: to collar someone is to catch them
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: Seize a ruler propping up American small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns COLLAR into RALLOC. The colon is misleading; 'in US' belongs with 'bit of change'.
explanation.definitionFit: Central locking is a car security system that locks all doors at once.

clue.text: Lean frames revealed, fashionable according to custom

indicators.note: frames means the first word surrounds the others like a picture frame

parts.note: to lean on someone is to rely on them
out means made public, revealed
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: Gaunt figures are exposed as the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like an adjective about thin frames but is the verb, giving RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something routinely means doing it as a matter of habit or custom.

clue.text: Committee not interested in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word for uninterested is to be heard, not read

parts.note: someone not interested is bored

explanation.surface: A committee comes across as dull when it talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A board is a governing committee, as in a board of directors.

clue.text: Good knight in power with attractive quality

indicators.note: in means the knight's letter sits inside the word for power

parts.note: beef is muscle, physical power
N is the chess notation for a knight
it is sex appeal, an attractive quality

explanation.surface: A virtuous knight is strong and charismatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage, something for one's good, as in 'for the good of all'.

clue.text: Distress induced shot

parts.note: to distress is to hurt
led means guided or induced

explanation.surface: Anguish caused someone to be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as gunfire but means moved very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurtled and shot both mean moved at great speed.

clue.text: Disorganised artiste was deprived of regular parts

indicators.note: losing every other letter leaves the alternate letters remaining

explanation.surface: A disorganised performer was stripped of key roles.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike out the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of ARTISTEWAS and the odd ones remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at sea is an idiom for being confused and disorganised.

clue.text: Biscuits? Horse tucked into a dry one

indicators.note: tucked into means the animal goes inside the other letters

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry, abstaining from drink
a mare is a female horse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asks whether biscuits are what a horse eats when tucked into a dry one.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretti are small Italian almond biscuits; the question mark flags the foreign plural.

clue.text: People in rising number led by resolve to show talent

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, one's resolve

indicators.note: in means the people go inside the number
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: two is a number
men are people

explanation.surface: Determination puts people among the top numbers, displaying ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' here is a noun, purpose or aim, not the verb; 'led by' puts it in front, and 'rising' flips the number upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a natural gift or talent.

clue.text: Will composer try album-oriented rock? That'll consume time

parts.note: to test is to try

indicators.note: That'll consume means the rock genre swallows the time letter

parts.note: AOR is album-oriented rock, a radio format

explanation.surface: Will a songwriter attempt rock music if it takes time?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will composer' looks like a question about whether someone will compose; it means someone who writes a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so a will composer.

clue.text: Inflexible artist keeping constant and not going back

indicators.note: going back reverses the whole assembled string of letters
keeping means the painter's name holds the other letters within

parts.note: Dali was the Spanish surrealist artist
C is the standard symbol for a constant, e.g. the speed of light
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A stubborn painter sticks to one idea and won't retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' makes DALCNORI, which 'going back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclad means rigid and unbreakable, as in an ironclad guarantee: inflexible.

clue.text: Trendy outfit with hot style

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A fashionable outfit with a sizzling look.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is informal for fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: Achieve advantage, getting opener out for duck

parts.note: to do is to accomplish or achieve

indicators.note: getting opener out drops the first letter, a cricket image of losing an opening batsman

parts.note: an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Gaining the upper hand when the opening batsman is out for nought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' sounds like a cricket score of zero but is the verb. EDGE without its first letter gives DGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck and to dodge both mean to evade or avoid.

clue.text: Food-related journal that's entertaining and in French

indicators.note: entertaining means holding, so the journal contains the French word

parts.note: a diary is a journal
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A food diary that's fun to read and written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary means relating to diet, the food one eats.

clue.text: Card game, very loud, not close

parts.note: faro is an old gambling card game
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A noisy card game that isn't intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-off means distant, the opposite of close.

clue.text: Pure displeasure when resistance is abandoned before defeat, nearly

indicators.note: is abandoned means the letter for resistance is dropped from the word

parts.note: anger is displeasure
R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to lick is to beat or defeat

explanation.surface: Annoyance as opposition is given up just before a near loss.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGER loses R to give ANGE; LICK nearly gives LIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means innocent and virtuous, as pure as an angel.

clue.text: Woodworm? Particular vault has got it

indicators.note: has got it means the answer is held within the run of words

explanation.surface: A woodworm has got into a particular vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: a woodworm is a beetle grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodworm is the larva of the furniture beetle, so an example of a larva.

clue.text: Group including bird of inferior status

indicators.note: including means the group word contains the bird

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
a wren is a small bird

explanation.surface: A flock containing a lowly bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-rent means cheap and second-rate, so of inferior status.

clue.text: External path, first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: a route is a path

explanation.surface: An outside track, going from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer and external both mean on the outside.

clue.text: Clumsy one after deductions accepting erroneous angle

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: accepting means the net amount takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: net means what remains after deductions

indicators.note: erroneous means wrong, so the letters of angle are rearranged

explanation.surface: An awkward figure after tax takes the wrong angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one after deductions' looks like a single idea, but 'one' and 'after deductions' are separate pieces; 'erroneous' jumbles angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace, awkward and clumsy.

clue.text: Dance lover with degree of proficiency and energy

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or lover
a dan is a grade of proficiency in martial arts
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: A dance enthusiast who is skilled and energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance for couples.

clue.text: One likely to carry on being stumped by philosopher

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Someone who persists despite being baffled by a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is someone with stamina who keeps going to the end.
